chapter_title: Concerning why if a [Nail] is cut the Person shall

spiritual_reading.full_translation: You know that the outward level of a person is the ultimate plane where inner things come to fixed form, and that the powers belonging to that outward level are the varied faculties and perceptions that rise within it. Among these faculties there are many kinds. Some arise from interior life, are restored again after loss, and are made stable in use, because their vitality is not merely from the outer plane but from what is living within. Others appear and function for a time, yet when they are deprived of what sustains them they do not return, because they have no inward root in living truth. There are also intermediate states that seem to be removed and then return, because some remnant of inward life still remains; and there are other states that, once destroyed, cannot be restored, because they never had genuine life in them. When the outward self takes delight in what is defiled, it grows strong in disorder and draws its vitality from impurity. Then the outer life becomes corrupted, and this corruption passes over into what ought to be living in the person, so that the healthier faculties are weakened and the whole state becomes sick.

paragraph_translations.translation: You know that the outward level of a person is the ultimate plane where inner things take form, and that the powers of that outward level are like the many faculties and perceptions that rise within it. These faculties are of many kinds. Some arise from interior life, return again after loss, and are made stable in use, because their vitality is not merely from what is outer but from what is living within. Others, when deprived or cut off, do not return, because they have no inward root in living truth. There are also mixed states that are removed and yet appear again, because something of inward life still remains; and there are other states that, once broken, do not revive, because they were never joined to what is living. When the outward self takes pleasure in what is defiled, it grows strong in disorder and draws its nourishment from impurity. Then the outer life becomes corrupt, and that corruption passes into what should be living in the person, so that the living faculties are weakened and become spiritually sick.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS the teaching by distinguishing faculties that can be restored from those that cannot, and then shifting to how delight in impurity spreads corruption inward.
paragraph_translations.notes: The source text is damaged and repetitive (several phrases break off), so the distinctions among the different kinds of faculties are partly uncertain; the final movement—impurity strengthening the outward self and corruption spreading into living faculties—reads coherently.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Coherent overall as one teaching: restoration depends on whether an outer faculty is rooted in inward life, and delight in impurity corrupts the outward self and then infects what should be living. The middle distinctions fragment slightly due to textual damage, but they still hold together as a graded set of recoverable vs. unrecoverable states.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential setup. The teaching proceeds by FUNCTION and organic analogy: the body is a ground-plane; limbs/faculties are growths that can be cut and may or may not regenerate depending on whether they have an inner root/life-source.
findings.evidence: Text: “the body is like the earth… these limbs… are like the trees… There are varieties of tree… Some… if they are cut shall… grow again… Again, there are others that if they are cut shall not [grow again]… They have not [their root in the earth].” The spiritual reading did not stumble here; it derived the spiritual sense from the functional distinction (regenerative vs non-regenerative growth) and explicitly grounded it in ‘root’/‘inward life.’ This is exactly the substrate’s mode: correspondence by growth/function, not by jurisdiction or named ranks.

findings.diagnosis: Genuine difficulty from damage and duplication, not an intrusive administrative overlay. The narrative ‘graded set’ is intact in intention (several kinds of cut-and-return vs cut-and-not-return), but the manuscript has overlapping phrases and torn syntax that make the enumeration stumble.
findings.evidence: Text shows repeated restarts and contradictions likely caused by lacunae: “They ar[is]e and grow again… They have not [their root in the earth] Again, there are others that if they are cut shall not [grow again] and they grow, as they are li[ke the reeds] which shall be cut and grow [again] and [others]… shall be cut and not grow… resembling [like the dry trees…].” The spiritual reading notes: “source text is damaged and repetitive… distinctions… partly uncertain,” yet it still reads the segment as a single continuum of recoverable/unrecoverable faculties. Removing any of these lines would not clearly restore a different ‘voice’; it would just shorten an already-fragmentary list.

findings.diagnosis: Clean continuation and moral application in the same correspondential voice. The passage pivots from the plant-regeneration analogy to the mechanism of corruption as a ‘nourishment’ taken from impurity, which then infects ‘living flesh’—still functional/organic causality, not administration.
findings.evidence: Text: “it [sh]all please him on [what is defiled] and grows [strong in it] in impurity [and draws nourishment] from him. This flesh that is corrupt [and its corruption passes over] in the liv[in]g flesh… [they] become weak… sick.” The spiritual reading confirms coherence here: “final movement… reads coherently,” describing exactly this functional spread (delight → nourishment → corruption → weakening/sickness). No named powers, jurisdictions, or inventories appear.

textual_criticism.summary: No administrative intrusions detected. 3 findings: 2 clean correspondential confirmations (opening analogy; closing corruption mechanism) and 1 genuine-difficulty diagnosis due to textual damage/duplication in the middle plant-type enumeration. Recommendations: excise 0, annotate 0, none 3.

harmonized_paragraphs.text: Happen you know th[at the] body is like the earth, wh[ile these] limbs als[o also] of it are like the trees. There are varieties [of] of tree you shall find growing on the earth. They ar[is]e and grow again and stand firm. They have not [their root in the earth] Again, there are others that if they are cut shall not [grow again] and they grow, as they are li[ke the reeds] which shall be cut and grow [again] and [others] they too that occur [upon the earth] they shall be cut and not grow, resembling [like the dry trees that neither] grow nor shall they [put forth shoot] it [sh]all please him on [what is defiled] and grows [strong in it] in impurity [and draws nourishment] from him. This flesh that is corrupt [and its corruption passes over] in the liv[in]g flesh and they [become weak and] are somewhat sick.

changes_summary: No changes made. All findings (1–3) carried a 'none' recommendation, with no excisions or annotations required.
